sources.title: OpenAI: MentalHealthBench open benchmark (Sep 23)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: OpenAI released MentalHealthBench on Sep 23: open benchmark for AI responses in realistic mental-health conversations, co-created with 80+ licensed psychologists/psychiatrists across 22 countries, 19 languages, ~20 subspecialties.

Design: 1,215 synthetic privacy-preserving conversations; acuity spectrum non-acute/high-acuity/emergencies; personas adults/teens/caregivers/clinicians, multilingual; rubric criteria weights -10..+10, each reviewed by >=3 experts, retained on >=2-expert agreement without third-expert contradiction.

Automated grader is GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI model grading OpenAI benchmark): methodology circularity risk explicitly flagged; side study of 44 adults (non-acute only) found users value tone/next-steps while experts emphasize context-seeking.
claims.context: Grader identity vendor-disclosed; circularity is an analytical boundary, not a vendor admission.

limitations.text: Paper-level methodology (agreement stats, grader validation) not consumed: no deep methodological verdict.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Comparative model readings are vendor-framed given grader overlap.
